q: Frank Clarke’s early-twentieth-century alarm-clock machine could wake its owner and automatically prepare which drink?
d: Its mechanism could strike a match, heat a kettle and pour the water. The device was an early ancestor of the electric Teasmade.
s: Science Museum Group · Automatic tea-making machine
evidence: Museum catalog details alarm clock,kettle tilter and spirit stove,with arm striking match,boiling kettle and pouring; explicitly calls early teasmade.

q: Which birds were fitted with tiny automatic cameras for an unusual form of early aerial photography?
d: A harness carried the camera during flight. The International Spy Museum displays a replica of a German pigeon-camera setup dated 1917–1918.
evidence: Museum object identifies replica German pigeon camera1917–18 and automatic photos in flight; avoids strong wartime-success and mission-rate claims.

q: An object in the Met’s library imitates a small decorated book. When its hidden mechanism runs, what rises from inside?
d: A hidden mechanism makes the bird turn and move its wings, tail and beak while producing birdsong. It retreats when the performance ends.
s: Metropolitan Museum of Art · Singing bird box in book form
evidence: Holding library describes silver and feather bird box mimicking leather bookbinding,with bird emerging,moving and singing before returning.

q: How did an operator choose a letter on a Mignon index typewriter, which lacked a normal alphabet keyboard?
d: A separate key printed the selected character. Replacing the chart and matching type sleeve could change the font or language.
choices: Setting a row of numbered levers
evidence: Catalog describes pointer over index card plus printing key; replaceable index/type sleeve changesfont/language. Ignores erroneous treaty date/world-war paragraph.

q: An Austrian alarm clock in the Science Museum’s fire-making collection is coupled to a tinder pistol. Besides sounding the alarm, what could it light?
d: The clock released the flintlock trigger, turning a time signal into a source of bedside light.
s: Science Museum Group · Tinder-pistol alarm clock
evidence: Holding museum explicitly says alarm releases trigger and candle lights. No operational or construction instructions.

q: Some twentieth-century shoe shops used a pedoscope to look at customers’ feet with what?
d: The machines showed foot bones inside shoes. Their use declined because of radiation concerns, despite little evidence that they improved shoe fitting.
s: Science Museum Group · Shoe-fitting X-ray viewer
evidence: Museum describes foot-bone and shoeoutline images and withdrawal with exposure-risk concerns; doesnot claim medically useful or safe.

q: On Philip Lea’s pocket globe from around 1700, Earth fits inside a small case. What is mapped on the inside of that case?
d: The tiny portable object pairs a terrestrial sphere with a colored map of the heavens surrounding it.
s: Royal Museums Greenwich · Philip Lea pocket globe
evidence: Object catalog explicitly describes colored constellations inside the case and terrestrial sphere, circa1700.

q: Why were the BBC’s original Concert Hall chairs heavily upholstered even where no audience member was sitting?
d: The padded seats helped reduce how much the room’s reverberation changed as the audience size changed.
s: Science Museum Group · BBC Concert Hall seating
evidence: Holding museum explains heavyupholstery absorption mitigates acoustic effect of changing audience numbers.
